edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from volume 1 of the Complete Works of Lu Xun (1948 printing); first published in New Youth (新青年), vol. 6, 1919, and collected in Call to Arms (吶喊), 1923.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自《鲁迅全集》第一卷（1948 年印本）；初刊于 1919 年《新青年》第六卷，收入《呐喊》（1923）。

basis.en: First published in 1919; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1919 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: A failed scholar who drinks his wine standing in a long gown, the only customer who does, and who is laughed at until one day he simply stops coming. Lu Xun tells it through a bored twelve-year-old serving boy, which is what makes it so hard to read: the boy laughs too. Notice the board where his debt is chalked; nineteen coppers are the last trace he leaves.
note.zh: 一个没有进学的读书人，是酒店里唯一站着喝酒而穿长衫的人，被众人取笑，直到有一天不再来。鲁迅借一个无聊的十二岁小伙计来讲，这正是它难读的地方：孩子也跟着笑。留意那块记账的粉板，十九个钱是他留下的最后痕迹。

excerpt.orig: 孔乙己是這樣的使人快活，可是沒有他，別人也便這麽過。
excerpt.en: That was how Kong Yiji made people happy, but without him, they got along just as well.
excerpt.zh: 孔乙己是这样的使人快活，可是没有他，别人也便这么过。
